claims: Measles is caused by the measles virus.
Measles spreads via airborne droplets when an infected person breathes, coughs, or sneezes.
Initial symptoms of measles include a high fever, runny nose, cough, and red, watery eyes.
Small white spots (Koplik spots) may appear inside the mouth 2-3 days after symptoms start.
A characteristic red, blotchy rash appears 3-5 days after initial symptoms.
The measles rash usually starts on the face and spreads downward.
The measles virus lives in the mucus of the nose and throat.
Measles often infects 90% of unvaccinated people close to an infected person.
The measles virus can remain active in the air or on surfaces for up to two hours.
Infected individuals can spread the measles virus four days before the rash appears.
Infected individuals can spread the measles virus up to four days after the rash appears.
Pneumonia is the most common cause of death from measles.
Measles complications include ear infections, diarrhea, pneumonia, and encephalitis.
Measles is most severe in infants, children under 5, adults over 20, and pregnant individuals.
There is no specific antiviral treatment for measles.
World Health Organization (WHO) recommends Vitamin A supplements for all children with acute measles.
Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommends two doses of the MMR (measles, mumps, and rubella) vaccine for children.
Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommends the first MMR vaccine dose between 12-15 months.
Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommends the second MMR vaccine dose between 4-6 years.
